NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Caregivers want a circle of families to help those recovering from illness: organize it, or let families help as they always have.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) has been looking after (friend.his/her) sick father alone for months and is exhausted. (subject) has an idea: a care circle, where families take turns bringing food, fetching water and sitting with the sick, so nobody carries it alone. Some families are already stretched thin. What should the village do?

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) sets up the circle. Every family takes a day. (friend) sleeps through a night for the first time in months. The circle costs the village food and time. Nobody regrets it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village helps as it always has: whoever notices, helps. Some weeks (friend) gets lots of help, some weeks none. (subject) brings soup every day anyway.
